name: straus_two_parameter_family

phase_0.boundary_condition: The terminal anchor ⊣ bounds the arithmetic constraint system over pairs (k, w) for fixed odd n ≡ 1 mod 24, containing all divisibility, coprimality, and congruence conditions that define valid pairs and their emptiness or least-k resolution.

VINIT.chosen_element: The void state before any pair (k, w) is named or tested
VINIT.justification: Before any positive integer pair is introduced, no divisibility or congruence condition has been evaluated; the register is void (00) and no parameter exists.

TANCH.chosen_element: The closed boundary of the constraint system over (k, w) for fixed n
TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor ⊣ contains the entire system of interdependent divisibility and congruence constraints that form a connected graph of relationships among k, w, and n.

AFWD.chosen_element: Forward morphism toward a valid pair (k, w) satisfying all constraints
AFWD.justification: The forward morphism → represents the directed transformation from candidate parameters toward a target pair that satisfies w | kn+1, gcd(w, 4k) = 1, k | w+1, and (w+1)/k ≡ 3 mod 4.

AREV.chosen_element: Reverse morphism descending through factorization of kn+1
AREV.justification: The reverse morphism ← represents the descent transformation through the factorization of kn+1, exploring divisor structure to find valid w values.

CLINK.chosen_element: Sequential chaining of divisibility and congruence checks
CLINK.justification: Composition ∘ chains the iterative cycles of factorization and congruence checks that propagate through the parameter space to explore valid (k, w) pairs.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: Self-reference of the constraint system on itself
IMSCRIB.justification: The identity id represents the system's self-recognition: the constraints on k and w are purely arithmetic and do not invoke any topological invariant, so the role carries no intrinsic protection.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: Splitting the parameter search into existence and emptiness branches
FSPLIT.justification: The co-multiplication δ opens the state into two arms: one exploring whether valid pairs exist (T-arm) and one determining whether the family is empty (F-arm).

FFUSE.chosen_element: Rejoining existence and emptiness determinations into a single verdict
FFUSE.justification: The multiplication μ reunites the T-arm (valid pairs found) and F-arm (family empty) into one B4 verdict, where conflicting arms rejoin to B if both states are held.

EVALT.chosen_element: Affirmative state: a valid pair (k, w) exists
EVALT.justification: The constructive truth T represents the affirmative arm where w divides kn+1, w is coprime to 4k, k divides w+1, and (w+1)/k ≡ 3 mod 4 are all satisfied.

EVALF.chosen_element: Negative state: no valid pair (k, w) exists
EVALF.justification: The constructive falsity F represents the negative arm where the family of pairs is empty, meaning no (k, w) satisfies all four arithmetic conditions simultaneously.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Paradise state: both existence and emptiness are simultaneously held
ENGAGR.justification: The B state holds both the affirmative (valid pairs exist) and negative (family is empty) simultaneously, a contradiction kept live without resolution, indicating critical behavior at the threshold.

IFIX.chosen_element: Permanent record of the least k when pairs exist
IFIX.justification: ROM fixation ◻ permanently records the least k value when the family is non-empty, an irreversible append-only record of the minimal solution.

phase_2.split_input: The initial parameter search state for pairs (k, w) under fixed odd n ≡ 1 mod 24
split_outputs: Existence branch: searching for valid (k, w) pairs satisfying all constraints
Emptiness branch: determining whether no valid pair exists
phase_2.fuse_result: A single B4 verdict over SIXTEEN_3: T if least k is found, F if family is empty, B if both states are held simultaneously
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: 00 — No pair (k, w) has been introduced; no divisibility, coprimality, or congruence condition has been evaluated.
phase_3.true_description: 01 — A valid pair (k, w) exists satisfying w | kn+1, gcd(w, 4k) = 1, k | w+1, and (w+1)/k ≡ 3 mod 4, with least k recorded.
phase_3.false_description: 10 — The family of pairs is empty; no (k, w) satisfies all four arithmetic conditions simultaneously for the given n.
phase_3.both_description: 11 — Paradice: both existence and emptiness are simultaneously held, indicating critical behavior where the system exhibits scale-free correlations and maximal sensitivity at the threshold.

steps.domain_action: The void state before any pair (k, w) is named or tested — register 00, no parameters exist.
The parameter search splits into two arms — T-arm for existence of valid pairs, F-arm for emptiness determination.

Forward morphism toward the target pair — directed transformation from candidate parameters to a valid (k, w) satisfying all constraints.
Sequential chaining of divisibility and congruence checks — composition ∘ propagates through iterative cycles of factorization and congruence verification.
The F-arm refutes constructive falsity — no valid pair (k, w) exists, the family is empty.
Reverse morphism descending through factorization of kn+1 — explores divisor structure to find valid w values, parity flip on the F-arm.
Paradice state — both existence and emptiness are simultaneously held, a contradiction kept live without resolution, indicating critical behavior.
Permanent ROM fixation — records the least k value when the family is non-empty, an irreversible append-only record.
The arms rejoin into one B4 verdict — T if least k is found, F if family is empty, B if both states are held simultaneously.
Terminal anchor ⊣ closes and contains the entire constraint system over (k, w) for fixed odd n ≡ 1 mod 24.

phase_6.post_cycle_state: After the cycle: the register holds the resolved B4 verdict (T, F, or B) with least k recorded in IFIX if existence was affirmed.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The cycle is entropy-conservative because the arithmetic constraints are purely structural and the register transitions are reversible information operations over SIXTEEN_3, with IFIX providing append-only records that do not dissipate entropy.
